properties.biography: Mike Hadreas, performing as Perfume Genius, began his music career in the late 2000s, releasing his debut album in 2010. Growing up in the United States, Hadreas developed a passion for music and songwriting, channeling his personal experiences and struggles into his art. Over the years, Perfume Genius has evolved from sparse, piano-driven ballads to more elaborate and experimental productions, gaining critical acclaim and a dedicated fanbase. His work is noted for its exploration of queer identity and emotional honesty.
properties.known_for: Perfume Genius is known for his emotionally raw and artfully crafted music that blends indie pop with experimental and baroque elements, as well as his candid exploration of queer identity and vulnerability.
properties.description: Perfume Genius is the musical project of Mike Hadreas, an American singer-songwriter and musician. Known for his deeply personal and emotionally charged lyrics, Hadreas blends elements of indie pop, art pop, and experimental music to create a unique sound characterized by lush arrangements and intimate vocal delivery. His work often explores themes of identity, vulnerability, and resilience, and he has been praised for his ability to convey complex emotions through his music.

properties.performance_style: Perfume Genius's performance style is intimate and emotionally expressive, often featuring minimalistic staging that focuses attention on the emotional delivery of his vocals and the nuanced instrumentation.

properties.biography: Dirty Projectors was formed in 2002 in Brooklyn, New York, by David Longstreth. Initially a solo project, it evolved into a full band with a rotating lineup of musicians. The band gained critical acclaim for their unique sound that combines indie rock with experimental and avant-garde influences. Their breakthrough album, "Bitte Orca" (2009), showcased intricate vocal harmonies and complex arrangements, earning them a dedicated following. Over time, the band has continued to push musical boundaries, incorporating diverse influences and maintaining a reputation for innovation in the indie music scene.

properties.biography: Erika M. Anderson grew up in the American Midwest and moved to Los Angeles at 18. She developed her distinctive experimental voice and guitar techniques playing in underground projects: she contributed to folk-noise outfit Amps for Christ in the late 1990s/early 2000s and co-founded the psych-folk band Gowns in 2004. After Gowns dissolved in 2010, Anderson began releasing solo material (Little Sketches on Tape, 2010) under the moniker EMA. Her 2011 single "Grey Ship" (which included an extended reinterpretation of Robert Johnson's "Kind Hearted Woman") and debut album Past Life Martyred Saints brought widespread critical attention and led to headline tours. She followed with The Future's Void (2014), an album and accompanying mixed-media work exploring technology and identity, and Exile in the Outer Ring (2017), a collaboration with Jacob Portrait addressing nationalism, poverty, and alienation in the U.S. Midwest. Anderson continues to work across music and visual art, collaborating with producers and scoring projects.
properties.known_for: Emotionally intense vocals, experimental guitar techniques, blending folk, noise and electronic production, and multidisciplinary projects that fuse music with visual art and immersive technology.
properties.description: EMA (Erika M. Anderson) is an American singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist whose work blends indie rock, electronic production and noise-informed folk. After cutting her teeth in underground acts such as Amps for Christ and psych-folk band Gowns, Anderson launched her solo project EMA around 2010. She gained critical acclaim with her 2011 debut Past Life Martyred Saints and broadened her palette on 2014's The Future's Void, exploring themes of virtual reality, consumerism and identity. Her work extends into visual and installation art (including an Oculus Rift-enabled exhibit at MoMA PS1 and the Barbican) and collaborative scoring, and she has toured extensively across North America and Europe.
properties.cultural_impact: EMA helped bring a confrontational, art-forward approach to indie music in the 2010s, crossing noise-folk, electronic and rock idioms while engaging contemporary topics like technology and identity. Critical acclaim for Past Life Martyred Saints established her as an influential voice in experimental indie; her MoMA PS1 and Barbican installations demonstrated a successful crossover between music and contemporary art, inspiring other musicians to pursue multimedia projects.
properties.performance_style: Live shows often mix direct, intimate vocal performance and guitar with layered electronics and visual elements; performances can feel confrontational and immersive, sometimes incorporating multimedia or installation components.

properties.biography: Formed in Brooklyn in 2002, Grizzly Bear began as Ed Droste's solo project before expanding into a full band when Daniel Rossen, Chris Taylor and Christopher Bear joined. They continued to evolve across Shields (2012) and Painted Ruins (2017), blending folk, chamber-pop and experimental production. Known for tight multi-part vocals and careful studio craft, the members also pursue side projects (Department Of Eagles, solo work) and production/engineering roles. The band has been largely inactive as a full touring unit since the late 2010s though its recordings remain influential in indie music.

properties.biography: Daniel Victor Snaith grew up in Dundas, Ontario. He began releasing music under the name Manitoba before changing to Caribou following a legal dispute; he later adopted the club alias Daphni for dancefloor-focused material. Snaith studied mathematics at the University of Toronto and completed a Ph.D. at Imperial College London in 2005 while continuing his musical career. His early Caribou albums—Start Breaking My Heart (folktronica/IDM), Up in Flames (shoegaze-infused electronica), and The Milk of Human Kindness (krautrock-influenced)—established him as an adventurous producer; Andorra (2007) broadened his profile after winning the 2008 Polaris Music Prize, and Swim (2010) marked a turn toward deeper, underwater-sounding dance music. Caribou's live performances are notable for their energy and visual design, frequently featuring multiple drummers and a band that brings his layered studio productions to the stage.

He first released full-length material under the Caribou name in the early 2000s (after initially recording as Manitoba), and is also known for his club-oriented work as Daphni. Snaith holds a Ph.D. in mathematics (Imperial College London, 2005) and is noted for evolving his sound across albums from the folktronica and jazz-inflected Start Breaking My Heart to the shoegaze-tinged Up in Flames, the krautrock-leaning The Milk Of Human Kindness, the Polaris Prize-winning pop-psychedelia of Andorra, and the disco-influenced Swim. His live shows mix live instrumentation (often with simultaneous drummers), sequenced electronics and synchronized visuals.

properties.biography: Beach House formed in Baltimore in 2004 when keyboardist–vocalist Victoria Legrand and guitarist–keyboardist Alex Scally began writing and performing together. properties.biography: Born July 1, 1975 in Detroit, Michigan, Sufjan Stevens grew up in a musical household in Michigan and began recording and self-releasing music in the late 1990s. He co-founded the Asthmatic Kitty label and gained international recognition with the 2003 album Michigan and the 2005 double-disc Illinois, part of his loose concept of state-themed recordings. properties.biography: Vulfpeck formed in 2011 after members met at the University of Michigan School of Music. Jack Stratton conceived the project as a modern, imagined version of classic 1960s American session groups (influenced by The Funk Brothers, The Wrecking Crew and Muscle Shoals) and focused on tight, minimal grooves and songcraft. Their catalog mixes instrumental showcases and soulful vocal tracks and features frequent collaborators from the modern funk and soul scene.

properties.biography: Mitski Miyawaki (born Mitsuki Laycock) was born in 1990 in Mie Prefecture, Japan, to a Japanese mother and an American father. Because her father worked for the U.S. Department of State, her family moved frequently and she spent parts of her childhood in Turkey, China, Malaysia, the Czech Republic and the Democratic Republic of Congo before ultimately moving to the United States. She sang in choirs in school and began composing on piano as a teenager. While studying studio composition at Purchase College, she self-released two albums, Lush (2012) and Retired from Sad, New Career in Business (2013), which began as senior projects. Mitski's breakthrough came with the rawer, guitar-forward Bury Me at Makeout Creek (2014). After signing to Dead Oceans she released Puberty 2 (2016), Be the Cowboy (2018) and Laurel Hell (2022), earning critical acclaim, festival headline slots and a growing global fanbase. In 2023 she released The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We. Her songwriting has been praised for its candor, dramatic dynamics and vivid, emotionally calibrated narratives.

Across subsequent releases she has continued to fuse folk-rooted songwriting with noisy, art-rock production and candid lyricism.

properties.biography: Dead & Company grew out of the continuing live-music legacy of the Grateful Dead after Jerry Garcia's death. In 2015 Bob Weir, Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann recruited John Mayer, Oteil Burbridge and Jeff Chimenti to form a working band that would perform extended, improvisational interpretations of Grateful Dead repertoire. Combining Mayer's contemporary pop-rock audience and guitar virtuosity with the rhythmic and improvisational DNA of the original Dead members, the group became a major touring act, known for multi-set concerts, fluid setlists and a culture of taping and community. Over multiple touring seasons they maintained the ritual of long-form jams while reintroducing classic material to new listeners; the band’s final scheduled touring run concluded in 2023.
properties.known_for: Live improvisational concerts that reinterpret the Grateful Dead songbook, long multi-set performances, and building a cross-generational community of fans.
properties.description: Dead & Company was formed in 2015 when former Grateful Dead members Bob Weir, Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann joined guitarist and singer John Mayer, along with Oteil Burbridge (bass) and Jeff Chimenti (keyboards). The group focused on live performances of the Grateful Dead songbook, blending long-form improvisation, rock, blues and Americana. They toured widely from 2015 through a final concert run in 2023, drawing both long-time Deadheads and new, younger fans through John Mayer's mainstream profile and virtuosic guitar work.
properties.cultural_impact: Dead & Company helped sustain and expand the Grateful Dead's cultural legacy into the 21st century, introducing classic Dead songs to younger audiences through John Mayer's mainstream profile. They reinforced festival and taping cultures, kept long-form live improvisation commercially viable, and contributed to a revival and mainstreaming of the modern jam-band scene.
properties.performance_style: Long, multi-set concerts focused on extended improvisation and seamless segues between songs; setlists vary nightly and shows emphasize spontaneous group interplay and audience participation, continuing the Grateful Dead live tradition.

properties.vocals: Allison Russell's vocals are characterized by a warm, soulful mezzo-soprano tone with expressive phrasing and a dynamic range that conveys vulnerability and strength. She often incorporates folk and soul vocal stylings, delivering her lyrics with emotional intensity and clarity.
properties.biography: Allison Russell was born in Canada and grew up immersed in music and storytelling. She began her career as a member of various bands before establishing herself as a solo artist. Her music draws heavily on her personal experiences, including overcoming trauma and finding healing through art. Russell's work has been praised for its emotional depth and lyrical sophistication, making her a distinctive voice in contemporary folk and Americana music.
properties.known_for: Her poetic songwriting, emotive vocals, and blending of folk, Americana, and soul influences with themes of healing and resilience.
properties.description: Allison Russell is a Canadian singer-songwriter known for her rich blend of folk, Americana, roots, country, blues, and soul music. Her work is characterized by deeply personal and poetic lyrics, often exploring themes of trauma, healing, and resilience. She is acclaimed for her emotive vocal delivery and multi-instrumental talents, including banjo and guitar.
properties.cultural_impact: Allison Russell has been recognized for bringing attention to issues of trauma and healing through her music, influencing contemporary folk and Americana scenes with her honest storytelling and advocacy for marginalized voices.
properties.performance_style: Allison Russell's performance style is intimate and emotionally expressive, often creating a deep connection with her audience through storytelling and heartfelt delivery.

properties.vocals: Marc Rebillet's vocals are characterized by a versatile and expressive style that adapts to his improvisational performances. He uses his voice both melodically and rhythmically, often layering loops to create complex vocal arrangements. His vocal delivery ranges from soulful singing to comedic spoken word, showcasing a wide emotional and stylistic range.
properties.biography: Marc Rebillet was born in Dallas, Texas, and developed an interest in music and performance at a young age. He studied music and began experimenting with electronic instruments and looping technology. Rebillet gained popularity through his live-streamed performances on YouTube and social media, where he improvises songs based on audience suggestions and current events. His blend of funk, soul, and electronic music, combined with comedic and often explicit lyrics, has set him apart in the music industry. Over time, he has toured internationally and released several albums, building a dedicated fanbase.
properties.known_for: Marc Rebillet is known for his improvised live performances that combine electronic music, funk, and comedy, using looping technology and spontaneous lyrics to engage audiences.
properties.description: Marc Rebillet is an American electronic musician, singer, and YouTube personality known for his unique style of improvised live performances that combine elements of electronic music, funk, soul, and comedy. He often creates songs on the spot using loop stations, keyboards, and his voice, engaging audiences with humorous and spontaneous lyrics. His energetic and charismatic performances have garnered a large online following and have made him a notable figure in the contemporary electronic and improvisational music scenes.
properties.cultural_impact: Marc Rebillet has influenced the way electronic and improvisational music is performed and consumed, particularly through live streaming and social media platforms. His unique blend of comedy and music has inspired a new generation of performers to embrace spontaneity and audience interaction, expanding the boundaries of live electronic music performance.
properties.performance_style: Marc Rebillet's performance style is highly improvisational and interactive, often involving live looping and audience participation. His shows are energetic and charismatic, blending music and comedy in a spontaneous and engaging manner.

properties.vocals: A deep, reverb-forward baritone with a crooning, vibrato-tinged delivery; vocals emphasize dramatic phrasing, sustained notes and a cinematic, nostalgic tone rather than extreme range or melismatic runs.
properties.biography: Orville Peck is a Canadian country artist who cultivated a masked, enigmatic stage persona early in his career to separate public image from private life. He began releasing music in the late 2010s, quickly drawing notice for a baritone vocal style drenched in reverb and for blending classic country tropes with alternative and gothic influences. Peck's debut full-length album Pony (2019) established him within both indie and country circles; later releases continued to expand his sonic palette while foregrounding queer narratives, vintage country imagery and cinematic production. He tours internationally and is often cited for pushing boundaries of country music's imagery and inclusivity.
properties.known_for: A masked, fringed-cowboy persona, deep reverb-heavy baritone vocals, cinematic production, and bringing queer visibility and theatricality to contemporary country and Americana.
properties.description: Orville Peck is a Canadian singer-songwriter who combines classic country songwriting with alternative, gothic and cinematic production. Recognizable for his fringed mask, deep reverb-soaked baritone and theatrical cowboy aesthetic, he emerged in the late 2010s and gained attention for his debut full-length Pony (2019) and subsequent releases. Peck is openly gay and has been noted for bringing queer visibility and glam-styled theatricality to modern country and Americana scenes.
properties.cultural_impact: Orville Peck has raised the profile of queer representation within modern country and Americana, blending glam and gothic aesthetics with traditional country tropes; his masked persona and fashion-forward presentation have influenced how theatricality and identity can be integrated into contemporary country performance.
properties.performance_style: Stoic, cinematic live shows that mix classic country staging with dramatic visuals and a masked, enigmatic persona; performances emphasize mood, atmosphere and vintage-Western iconography.
